Case: Google and Apple sign-up buttons are displayed on both the login and sign-up identifier screens
Description:
• Pre-condition: User is on the sign-up identifier screen (sso.sleekflow.io/u/signup) and separately on the login identifier screen.
  • Source: sleekflow-login-signup-004 · AC1
Test Steps:
1. Navigate to the sign-up identifier screen.
  2. Observe the presence of Google and Apple buttons.
  3. Navigate to the login identifier screen.
  4. Observe the presence of Google and Apple buttons.
Expected:
• Both "Continue with Google" and "Continue with Apple" buttons are visible on the sign-up identifier screen.
  • Both buttons are also visible on the login identifier screen.
BDD: Given the user is on either the sign-up or login identifier screen, When the page loads, Then both Google and Apple social sign-in buttons are displayed

Case: Company setup screen is displayed after first-time Google sign-up
Description:
• Pre-condition: A Google account that has never been registered with SleekFlow is used. User is on the sign-up identifier screen.
  • Source: sleekflow-login-signup-004 · AC2
Test Steps:
1. Navigate to the sign-up identifier screen.
  2. Click "Continue with Google".
  3. Select or authenticate with a Google account not previously registered with SleekFlow.
  4. Complete the Google OAuth consent flow.
  5. Observe the page shown after OAuth completion.
Expected:
• User is redirected to the company setup screen (not the app dashboard).
  • No error message is shown.
BDD: Given a first-time Google user completes OAuth, When the OAuth flow returns to SleekFlow, Then the company setup screen is displayed

Case: App dashboard is displayed when a returning Google user signs in
Description:

  • Source: sleekflow-login-signup-004 · AC2
Test Steps:

  2. Click "Continue with Google".

  4. Complete the Google OAuth flow.
  5. Observe the page shown after OAuth completion.
Expected:
• User is redirected to the SleekFlow app dashboard (not company setup).
  • No error message is shown.
  • User is logged in as the expected account.
BDD: Given a returning Google user completes OAuth, When the OAuth flow returns to SleekFlow, Then the app dashboard is displayed

Case: No consent checkbox is shown on the social sign-up screen
Description:
• Pre-condition: User is on the sign-up identifier screen about to use Google or Apple sign-up.
  • Source: sleekflow-login-signup-004 · AC1
Test Steps:
1. Navigate to the sign-up identifier screen.
  2. Observe the area around the Google and Apple buttons.
  3. Check for the presence of any Terms/Privacy consent checkbox.
Expected:
• No consent checkbox is displayed adjacent to or below the Google/Apple buttons on the sign-up screen.
  • At most, implied consent text may appear (e.g., "By continuing, you agree to...") — but no interactive checkbox.
BDD: Given the user is on the social sign-up screen, When the page loads, Then no mandatory consent checkbox is displayed for Google or Apple sign-up

Case: Consent timestamp and Terms version are recorded after first-time social sign-in
Description:
• Pre-condition: A new Google or Apple account completes the sign-up flow and reaches the app. D2 decision is required — this TC is flagged Manual until Legal decides between implied consent text (a) or in-app checkbox (b).
  • Source: sleekflow-login-signup-004 · AC3
  • Note (D2 TBD): REQUIREMENT PENDING — consent mechanism not finalized. Test to be updated once Legal decision is made.
Test Steps:
1. Complete first-time social sign-up with a new Google or Apple account.
  2. Proceed through to the app (past company setup).
  3. If D2(b): confirm the in-app consent checkbox is shown and interact with it.
  4. If D2(a): confirm implied consent text is shown under the social buttons.
  5. Using an admin API or audit panel, check that a consent record was created for this user.
Expected:
• A consent record exists for the user with a timestamp matching the sign-up time.
  • The record includes the Terms version accepted.
  • EXPECTED (D2a): consent is implied via text shown before OAuth; record is created automatically.
  • EXPECTED (D2b): user must interact with checkbox on first in-app screen before proceeding; consent record is created on submission.
BDD: Given a first-time social user completes sign-up, When the user reaches the app, Then a consent record with timestamp and Terms version is captured per the agreed D2 mechanism

Case: Social sign-up behaviour when social email matches an existing password-based account is handled gracefully
Description:
• Pre-condition: A SleekFlow account exists with email address X using email/password login. User attempts to sign up or sign in using a Google or Apple account that uses the same email address X.
  • Source: sleekflow-login-signup-004 · AC2
  • Note (Open Item TBD): Behavior is unknown per ticket. This TC is flagged Manual and must be updated once behavior is defined.
Test Steps:
1. Confirm an existing SleekFlow account exists for email X (password-based).
  2. Navigate to the sign-up or login identifier screen.
  3. Click "Continue with Google" (or Apple) using an account with the same email X.
  4. Complete the OAuth flow.
  5. Observe the resulting screen and any error or routing behavior.
Expected:
• EXPECTED (to be defined): user receives a clear message indicating the email is already registered with a different method, with guidance to sign in via email/password or link accounts.
  • CURRENT: behavior is unknown — no duplicate account should be silently created.
BDD: Given an existing password-based account uses email X, When a social sign-up with the same email X is attempted, Then the user receives clear feedback and no duplicate account is created
